text: Hens start producing fertilizable eggs at 5–6 months of age. The ovary is a cluster of developing yolks; pullets carry 2,000 to 10,000 potential eggs. A yolk takes about 10 days to grow from very small to its normal size; it nourishes the developing chick and supplies maternal antibodies against infection. Yolk color depends on diet, especially pigments from corn. Ovulation — release of the mature yolk into the oviduct — occurs 30–60 minutes after the previous egg is laid, usually in the morning. The egg then passes through the oviduct: the infundibulum (where fertilization happens if sperm is present), the magnum (where albumen/egg white is added, about 3.5 hours), the isthmus (where shell membranes are added, about 1.5 hours), and the uterus (where the hard calcified shell forms, about 20 hours), which protects the egg and gives it a dark, warm, moist, sterile environment.
